title: Freely given (Matthew 10:1–15)
hookLine: freely you have received, freely give
tomorrow: how do you walk among wolves and stay gentle?

cards: Free trial, then the card gets charged. Free shipping over a certain total. Free is usually a hook.

Matthew uses the word another way. He stops to read out names: Simon called Peter, Andrew his brother, James and John, Matthew the publican, the tax collector from the booth, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
Twelve, given power to heal, and about to hear their one rule about money.

teach.b: Here it is: "Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give." The reason comes with the rule. Nothing they carry was bought, so none of it is for sale.
They aren't even allowed to pack: "Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses." And "the workman is worthy of his meat": the givers live on what others give them.
Free giving runs both ways: the people who give for nothing also receive for nothing.
If a house says no, "let your peace return to you." The peace isn't wasted; it comes home. So the question underneath: what do you owe for a gift?
Not a payment. A passing-on. This is shared ground with a neighbor.

teach.h: THE DHAMMAPADA: THE GIFT OF THE LAW.
teach.b: The Dhammapada, a collection of the Buddha's sayings, says in Max Müller's translation: "The gift of the law exceeds all gifts." Law there means the dhamma, the Buddha's teaching.
Both traditions put a teaching passed on near the top of what a person can give.
And one honest difference: the twelve pass on what they received from God, healing and the news that the kingdom of heaven is at hand; the Dhammapada's gift is the Buddha's own teaching, the dhamma.

how: Some Christians read Matthew 10 when sending out missionaries or volunteers, and some ministries offer their care free of charge, pointing to freely ye have received, freely give.

games.q: a tutor helped you through chemistry for free and won't take anything back. now a younger kid is drowning in the same class. what fits Matthew 10?
o: help the kid for free, the way you were helped.
charge the kid, since your time is worth something now.

games.why: freely ye have received, freely give. the gift isn't settled by paying it back; it goes on as a gift.

practice: Choose one thing to give away for nothing, and take the first step before the sit ends: set the book by the door, put the coat in a bag, write down whose afternoon gets your hour.
No receipt and no score, just something passing from your hands.
